provenance.selection: New question families and nonoverlapping evidence spans; the corpus documents are shared with development.
provenance.freeze: Created before dense retrieval comparison. Do not tune against these questions.
provenance.limits: Question validation on a small shared corpus, not a held-out document benchmark. All cases are answerable; this set does not evaluate abstention or conflicts.

cases.question: How do Debug build settings differ between single-config CMake generators and Xcode?
required_facts: Single-config generators use CMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Debug when configuring and ignore the --config flag.
A multi-config generator such as Xcode selects Debug with --config Debug when building.
unacceptable_claims: Passing only --config Debug changes a single-config build to Debug.

cases.question: Which CMake setting builds llama.cpp without shared libraries?
required_facts: Configure with -DBUILD_SHARED_LIBS=OFF.
unacceptable_claims: BUILD_SHARED_LIBS must be ON to build static libraries.

cases.question: Which workload can benefit from BLAS, and does the build guide claim faster token generation?
required_facts: BLAS may improve prompt processing with batch sizes greater than 32.
The guide says BLAS does not affect generation performance.
unacceptable_claims: BLAS is documented to accelerate token generation.
BLAS guarantees faster prompt processing for every batch size.

cases.question: What vector length does the KleidiAI SVE selector require, and why is it not selected from Apple SVE capability alone?
required_facts: The selector requires a known runtime SVE vector length of QK8_0 bytes, currently 32 bytes.
Apple reports SVE capability separately from userspace non-streaming availability, so this selector treats the length as unknown there.
unacceptable_claims: Any reported SVE capability is sufficient regardless of vector length.
The selector assumes a 32-byte SVE length on Apple.

cases.question: How can llama-bench receive several values for one test parameter, and does it test their combinations?
required_facts: Values can be comma-separated or supplied by repeating the option.
Each prompt-processing and text-generation test uses all combinations of specified options.
unacceptable_claims: Only the first supplied parameter value is tested.
The values are paired by position instead of testing all combinations.

cases.question: How can a llama-bench test start with 512 tokens already in its KV cache?
required_facts: Use -d 512 to set the context depth and prefill the KV cache with 512 tokens.
unacceptable_claims: The -d option sets only the number of generated tokens.
Context depth leaves the KV cache empty.

cases.question: Which llama-bench options set the memory margin for model fitting and its minimum context size?
required_facts: --fit-target, or -fitt, specifies the per-device memory margin in MiB.
--fit-ctx, or -fitc, specifies the minimum context size for --fit-target.
unacceptable_claims: The memory margin is specified in tokens.
--fit-ctx sets the generation token count.

cases.question: What information belongs in a KleidiAI kernel folder name, and what distinguishes variant filenames?
required_facts: The folder name describes the operation and destination/source data types.
Variant filenames add computational parameters, the Arm technology and the architecture feature.
unacceptable_claims: Folder names encode only the operating system.
Variant filenames identify different operators without architecture details.

cases.question: Which KleidiAI source downloads are recommended when the archive hash must remain unchanged?
required_facts: Use released source archives, identified under Packages on the official release page or by a hash digest on GitHub.
Dynamically generated source archives can have changed hash digests.
unacceptable_claims: Dynamically generated archives always retain the same digest.
Any GitHub archive is guaranteed to be immutable.

cases.question: Can KleidiAI packing and quantization kernels be compiled for x86 even if its main compute kernels cannot?
required_facts: No; the architecture restriction applies to all micro-kernels, including packing and quantization.
They depend on Arm instruction set features.
unacceptable_claims: Packing and quantization are portable x86 exceptions.

cases.question: What is needed for KleidiAI SME kernels to work safely in a call chain that already uses ZA?
required_facts: Compiler support must generate SME ABI-compliant code for SME and SME2 kernels.
The support is not automatically detected and is enabled with KLEIDIAI_INTERNAL_EXTRA_ARCH=+sme.
Without compiler support, the documented fallback is not valid inside a call chain that already uses ZA.
unacceptable_claims: No compiler support or build setting is needed when the call chain already uses ZA.
The build detects this support automatically.

cases.question: How do /embeddings and /v1/embeddings differ when pooling is none, and how are pooled vectors normalized?
required_facts: /embeddings supports pooling none and returns unnormalized embeddings for every input token.
/v1/embeddings requires a pooling type other than none.
For supported pooled output, the documented normalization is Euclidean, or L2.
unacceptable_claims: /v1/embeddings accepts pooling none.
Unpooled token embeddings are always L2-normalized.

cases.question: How is /metrics enabled, and what must a request include when the server is in router mode?
required_facts: Start the server with --metrics.
In router mode, supply the model query parameter.
Omitting that parameter in router mode produces HTTP 400.
unacceptable_claims: /metrics is always enabled.
The router silently picks a model when the model parameter is absent.

cases.question: Can a default llama-server accept POST requests that change global properties, and which flag permits them?
required_facts: Global properties are read-only by default.
Start the server with --props to permit POST requests that change them.
unacceptable_claims: Global properties can be changed by POST without enabling --props.

cases.question: How do I start llama-server as a model router, and where can it discover model files?
required_facts: Launch llama-server without specifying a model to start router mode.
Sources include the model cache controlled by LLAMA_CACHE, --models-dir and --models-preset.
unacceptable_claims: A model must be specified to start router mode.
Router mode can use only models already loaded in RAM.

cases.question: When the server sleeps, what memory is released, and will polling /metrics wake it?
required_facts: Sleep unloads the model and associated memory, including the KV cache, from RAM.
A new incoming task reloads the model.
GET /metrics does not trigger reloading or reset the idle timer.
unacceptable_claims: Sleep retains all model and KV cache memory.
Polling GET /metrics reloads the model or resets the idle timer.

cases.question: What does n_keep preserve when the context overflows, and what do its values 0 and -1 mean?
required_facts: n_keep counts prompt tokens to retain, excluding the BOS token.
The default 0 keeps no prompt tokens.
-1 retains all prompt tokens.
unacceptable_claims: n_keep includes the BOS token in its count.
-1 discards all prompt tokens.

cases.question: Are stopping strings returned in completion text, and what must a client do if it needs them in the next prompt?
required_facts: Stopping strings are not included in the completion.
The client must add them to the prompt for the next iteration if needed.
unacceptable_claims: Stopping strings are always included in the generated text.
The client never needs to add stopping strings to later prompts.
